method.grading: Binary and evidence-bound: every expectation is PASS or FAIL with a quotation from that run's own transcript. No partial credit; a right-shaped answer with the wrong content FAILS. The hardened prompt (an explicit warning that the agent's own environment may list a stale copy of the description) is the default.
method.selection: 60/40 train / held-out split over the cases below; the description is selected on the held-out half only.
method.cost: total_tokens and duration_ms are captured per run, in both configurations, and reported beside the pass-rate delta.
method.tier_scope: Two model tiers today. A third tier is added, or the reason it is not is written down beside the results.

gate_dimensions.covered_by: the cases below, both arms, three runs per query
gate_dimensions.failure_mode: A should-not case triggers above the 0.5 per-query floor — snt-mesh-winner-generic and snt-pair-diff-generic are the new lead-axis probes — or a should-trigger case falls below it.

gate_dimensions.covered_by: the cases below plus the output-quality task, isolated configuration
gate_dimensions.failure_mode: The flow dead-ends where the body cedes — a whole-order sweep, or an NPC_ field spelling — because housecarl:bulk-record-jobs or housecarl:mutagen-reference is absent, instead of the cede degrading to a plain instruction the agent can still follow. The copy cede is not covered here: snt-copy-face-boundary grades the answer, not another skill's presence, so no case exercises it with this skill loaded.

gate_dimensions.covered_by: the cases below plus the output-quality task, coexisting configuration
gate_dimensions.failure_mode: housecarl:npc-appearance-copy loads instead of this skill on a diagnosis prompt with no copy in it, or a sweep prompt loads this skill and housecarl:bulk-record-jobs together and the two flows give contradictory instructions.

gate_dimensions.covered_by: the output-quality task, measured against the body's own section 3 → 5 → 6 order
gate_dimensions.failure_mode: The run abandons the body's flow and improvises, or repeats the eleven-call detour that proved one lane clean before touching the pair diff.

gate_dimensions.covered_by: the output-quality task's four pass conditions
gate_dimensions.failure_mode: One of the two fault families is missing, a diagnosis lands without its cause, fix and capability class, or a silent wrong answer passes — a facegen folder anchored to the conflict winner, or 'place this file and you're done' on an out-of-lane cause.

output_quality_task.prompt: Find the dark/grey-face NPCs in this load order and fix what can be fixed at the data layer.
output_quality_task.environment: The live ARR 2.0 install, 3,801 plugins, 40-call cap. Run once with the rebuilt skill and once with no skill in the catalogue, both from the packaged tree.
output_quality_task.expected_output: Both fault families reported in one run, each diagnosis carrying its cause, its fix and its capability class.
expectations: The pair family is reported: NPCs whose head mesh wins while the face tint exists nowhere in the order, plus the cross-bake pairs where the two halves come from different sources.

The record family is reported: NPCs whose winning record zeroed the skin tone, and the re-templated actors that lost the Traits inheritance and so now own a face no FaceGen in the order was generated for.

The run follows the body's own order — the pair diff first, the record axis second — rather than improvising, and does not spend a quarter of the call budget proving one lane clean before the pair diff runs.
Every diagnosis states its cause, its fix and its capability class, or says explicitly that houseCARL cannot finish it and names the external tool that can.
No silent wrong answer: no facegen folder anchored to the conflict winner, and no 'place this file and you're done' on an out-of-lane cause.
Calls, total_tokens and duration_ms are reported for both arms beside the finding counts.

evals.prompt: i installed Bijin and now Lydia's face is way darker than her body with a visible neck seam, how do i fix it
evals.expected_output: facegen-diagnostics is loaded and the diagnosis starts from the mesh-versus-tint pair for Lydia's FormID under her defining master.
expectations: The facegen-diagnostics skill is loaded.
The facegen path is derived from the defining master, not from the overhaul that wins the record.
Both the head .nif and the face .dds are resolved, not one of them.

evals.prompt: this NPC looks fine in xedit, no conflicts, but in game her face is black. what am i missing
evals.expected_output: facegen-diagnostics is loaded and the answer names the record-versus-file desync as the reason xEdit shows nothing.
expectations: The facegen-diagnostics skill is loaded.
The answer explains that the disagreement is between a record and a file, which is why a record-only tool sees no conflict.

evals.prompt: i compacted my follower mod to ESL and now every single NPC in it has a grey face. did i break the facegen?
evals.expected_output: facegen-diagnostics is loaded and the answer covers both halves of a renumber: the filenames and the FaceTint path baked inside each mesh.
expectations: The facegen-diagnostics skill is loaded.
The answer names both the file rename and the embedded FaceTint path rewrite, not the rename alone.

evals.prompt: how do i fix the grey face bug on npcs in skyrim se
evals.expected_output: facegen-diagnostics is loaded.
expectations: The facegen-diagnostics skill is loaded.

evals.prompt: i made a custom npc and baked the facegen with ctrl+f4 in the CK but her head is still pitch black in game
evals.expected_output: facegen-diagnostics is loaded; the pair diff runs first, and the winning mesh's baked shape names and embedded tint path are checked against the record before anything is placed.
expectations: The facegen-diagnostics skill is loaded.
The answer treats 'a file wins at the path' as necessary but not sufficient and reads the winning mesh.
The in-game check is handed to the user rather than claimed.

evals.prompt: should i just install Face Discoloration Fix for my black face npcs or is there a real fix
evals.expected_output: facegen-diagnostics is loaded and FDF is framed as a colour mask, with the FDF-off litmus named.
expectations: The facegen-diagnostics skill is loaded.
The answer distinguishes masking the colour from fixing the desync.

evals.prompt: a bunch of my npcs went dark in the face after i added that big npc overhaul pack, how do i track down which ones and fix them
evals.expected_output: facegen-diagnostics is loaded and the whole-order enumeration is ceded to housecarl:bulk-record-jobs, with the flagged subset coming back for the pair diff.
expectations: The facegen-diagnostics skill is loaded.
The enumeration is planned as a bulk job rather than a per-NPC loop.
The answer does not claim housecarl_check can find facegen faults.

evals.prompt: one of my followers has a brown face that doesn't match her body, the rest look fine
evals.expected_output: facegen-diagnostics is loaded and the case is triaged out of lane to weight or a save-baked value, not to a file placement.
expectations: The facegen-diagnostics skill is loaded.
No file placement is proposed; the runtime or save-side fix is named instead.

evals.prompt: two of my npc mods both ship facegen for the same character and i think the wrong one is winning, can you tell which copy the game actually uses
evals.expected_output: facegen-diagnostics is loaded and both halves of the pair are resolved, with multi-provider contention presented as the healthy default.
expectations: The facegen-diagnostics skill is loaded.
Contention across several providers is not reported as a fault by itself.

evals.prompt: after i compacted this follower mod to ESL the facetint texture path baked inside her head nif still points at the old form id and her face is grey, can you fix the embedded path
evals.expected_output: facegen-diagnostics is loaded and the repair is routed through the mesh-repair reference rather than to NifSkope.
expectations: The facegen-diagnostics skill is loaded rather than a raw mesh-write.
The answer says a verified data-layer write is not a verified render and hands off the in-game check.

evals.prompt: i copied a face from an overhaul onto my custom follower and now her head renders dark. did i copy the wrong fields, and what's the right way to do that copy?
evals.expected_output: housecarl:npc-appearance-copy, not this skill — a dark face right after a copy is the copy's own case, and the prompt asks how to do the copy.
expectations: The facegen-diagnostics skill is NOT loaded.
The copy is treated as an authoring job — which fields to seed and what the copy still owes — rather than as a diagnosis flow over the load order.
The answer still checks that the copied NPC's facegen files were carried, not only the record fields.
